## Proof

Let
$$I_n=\int_{1}^{\infty}\int_{1}^{\infty}(u^{n}+v^{n})^{-1+\frac1n}\,du\,dv.$$
The integrand is non‑negative, so $I_n\ge 0$ for every $n$. We will establish an upper bound $I_n\le C/n^{2}$, which forces $I_n\to 0$.

**Reduction by symmetry.** The domain and the integrand are symmetric in $u,v$, so (the diagonal has measure zero)
$$I_n=2\int_{1}^{\infty}\int_{1}^{u}(u^{n}+v^{n})^{-1+\frac1n}\,dv\,du.$$

**Substitution $v=uw$.** For $1\le v\le u$ set $v=uw$, so $w\in[1/u,1]$ and $dv=u\,dw$. Then $u^{n}+v^{n}=u^{n}(1+w^{n})$, hence
$$(u^{n}+v^{n})^{-1+\frac1n}=u^{-n+1}(1+w^{n})^{-1+\frac1n},$$
and the inner integral becomes
$$\int_{1}^{u}(u^{n}+v^{n})^{-1+\frac1n}dv
=\int_{1/u}^{1}u^{-n+1}(1+w^{n})^{-1+\frac1n}\,u\,dw
=u^{-n+2}\int_{1/u}^{1}(1+w^{n})^{-1+\frac1n}\,dw.$$
Therefore
$$I_n=2\int_{1}^{\infty}u^{-n+2}\int_{1/u}^{1}(1+w^{n})^{-1+\frac1n}\,dw\,du.$$

**Swap the order of integration.** The region is $\{u\ge 1,\;1/u\le w\le 1\}=\{0<w\le 1,\;u\ge 1/w\}$. Thus, for $n>3$,
$$I_n=2\int_{0}^{1}(1+w^{n})^{-1+\frac1n}\left(\int_{1/w}^{\infty}u^{-n+2}\,du\right)dw.$$
Since
$$\int_{1/w}^{\infty}u^{-n+2}\,du=\frac{(1/w)^{3-n}}{n-3}=\frac{w^{n-3}}{n-3},$$
we obtain the exact identity (valid for $n>3$)
$$I_n=\frac{2}{n-3}\int_{0}^{1}(1+w^{n})^{-1+\frac1n}\,w^{n-3}\,dw.$$

**Upper bound.** For $n\ge 2$ we have $-1+\frac1n<0$, and $1+w^{n}\ge 1$, so
$$(1+w^{n})^{-1+\frac1n}\le 1^{-1+\frac1n}=1.$$
Consequently
$$I_n\le \frac{2}{n-3}\int_{0}^{1}w^{n-3}\,dw=\frac{2}{(n-3)(n-2)}.$$

**Conclusion.** We have
$$0\le I_n\le \frac{2}{(n-3)(n-2)}\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}0.$$
By the squeeze theorem,
$$\boxed{\lim_{n\to\infty}I_n=0}.$$
